intro: Day 1 of SSC CGL 2026 Tier 1 ran in two slots, 1:30 PM and 5:00 PM. The 10 AM slot had no exam at virtually every centre. This was also the first CGL with a locked 15-minute timer for each section, and that timer drew more comment than any single question. The 1:30 PM paper was easy to moderate. The 5:00 PM paper was a notch harder, with a data-interpretation set in Quant and a tougher English section.

shifts.note: No SSC CGL paper was conducted in the 10 AM slot on 30 September at almost all centres. Some reviewers say no candidates were allotted to it, while others describe it as cancelled. SSC has not issued a statement either way. Videos and pages titled '30 September Shift 1' are almost always about the 1:30 PM paper, which was the first one actually held.

shifts.alsoCalled: Some coaching sites and YouTube channels call this the 'Shift 1' paper, because it was the first shift actually held on 30 September. It is the same exam.
shifts.summary: The paper leaned heavily on previous-year question patterns. Reasoning and English were comfortable for most candidates. General Awareness felt harder than its content because of statement-based and chronology questions. Quant was mostly direct formula work in advanced maths. The 15-minute lock, not the questions, is what set the pace: several candidates had solvable questions still open when the Quant timer ran out.

sections.name: General Intelligence & Reasoning
sections.notes: Most questions were standard types. There were one or two unfamiliar coding questions, and two statement-conclusion items that were not syllogisms and took time.

sections.name: General Awareness
sections.notes: Many questions were statement-based, assertion-reason or order-the-events items, and those made the section feel tougher than its facts were. There were about 4–5 current-affairs questions.

sections.name: Quantitative Aptitude
sections.notes: About 14–16 of the 25 questions were advanced maths. Most could be solved with a formula in one or two lines. A few arithmetic questions were calculation-heavy, and those are where the 15-minute timer hurt.

topics.topic: Mensuration – pyramid, cone, hexagon in circle

sections.name: English Comprehension
sections.notes: Candidates found this section long rather than hard. The reading passage came first, and several reviewers said it closely resembled a passage from CGL 2025. Almost all the vocabulary had appeared in earlier papers.

asked.q: If tan A + cot A = 2, find the value of tanⁿA + cotⁿA for a high power n.
A simple-interest question comparing the amount after 3 years with the amount after 5 years, where you work back to the principal and rate.
Two equal parallel chords of a circle a given distance apart: find the radius or the chord length.
Volume of a pyramid with a square base, given the base side and slant height.
Length of the direct or transverse common tangent between two circles, given their radii and the distance between centres.
Put in chronological order: setting up of the Inter-State Council, the 73rd Constitutional Amendment, and the launch of GST.
Which pollutants are counted in India's National Air Quality Index?
asked.a: Eight: PM10, PM2.5, NO₂, SO₂, CO, O₃, NH₃ and lead

asked.q: An assertion-reason pair on Humayun's Tomb and its charbagh (four-part garden) layout.
A question on the Gandhara school of art and the influences that shaped it.
asked.a: Greco-Roman style fused with Buddhist themes

asked.q: Which layer of the Earth lies directly below the lithosphere and is partly molten?
Which four countries make up the QUAD grouping?
asked.a: India, the USA, Japan and Australia

asked.q: Meaning or synonym items on previous-year words such as 'logorrhoea' (excessive talk), 'supercilious' (arrogantly superior) and 'equanimity' (calmness).
Meaning of the idiom 'keep one's head above water'.
asked.a: To just manage to survive, especially financially

observations: The locked 15-minute timer for each section was the main talking point after the exam. Some called it fair because it applies to everyone. Others said it cut off solvable Quant questions.
The section order most candidates reported was Reasoning, then GA, then Quant, then English, with no choice. One candidate said Quant came first at their centre.
No technical glitches were reported from this shift.
Across all four sections the paper stayed close to previous-year question types, so candidates who had practised past papers were rewarded.
disagreements: GA good attempts: coaching tables put them at 22–23, but most video reviews suggest 12–18 is more realistic. We show 15–18.
Quant: some reviewers called it easy and formula-based, with 22–25 possible. Others called it calculation-heavy and put average attempts at 15–18. We show 20–23 for a well-prepared candidate.
Overall difficulty: one live analysis page changed its overall rating from Easy-Moderate to Moderate during the evening. Most other sources said Easy-Moderate.

sources.name: Gagan Pratap Maths – Shift 2 student reviews (YouTube)

shifts.alsoCalled: Some sites list this 5 PM paper as 'Shift 2', because only two shifts were held on 30 September.
shifts.summary: This paper was harder than the 1:30 PM one. Quant included a graph-based data-interpretation set with heavy calculation, which most reviewers advised skipping under the 15-minute lock. English was long, with a demanding cloze test, para-jumbles and error spotting. Reasoning stayed easy to moderate, and General Awareness was mostly direct one-line facts. Repeat candidates rated it moderate, while first-timers found it tough.

sections.name: General Intelligence & Reasoning
sections.notes: Mostly standard types. This shift had more figure-based questions than the 1:30 PM paper, and some candidates skipped them to save time.

sections.name: General Awareness
sections.notes: The section was mostly factual, with few statement-based questions. That made it quick if you knew the fact, but left little room to eliminate options if you didn't. There were about 3–4 current-affairs questions.

sections.name: Quantitative Aptitude
sections.notes: This was the hardest section of the shift. A graph-based data-interpretation set (about 4–5 questions, per one candidate) appeared for the first time this cycle, and the arithmetic was calculation-heavy. Most reviewers suggested skipping DI and banking on the advanced-maths questions.

sections.name: English Comprehension
sections.notes: Several reviewers called this the toughest English section of the day, mainly because of its length. The cloze test, the para-jumbles and the error-spotting questions all needed careful reading.

asked.q: How many points is a touchdown worth in American football?
Where was the 2023 World Test Championship final played?
Who wrote 'Heat and Dust', the 1975 Booker Prize winner?
Which Article of the Constitution provides for a financial emergency?
Teej is mainly associated with which season?
A question on India's medallists in shooting at the 2026 Asian Games.
A question on the reforms introduced by Governor-General William Bentinck.
A 4–5 question data-interpretation set built on a graph, with the answers requiring percentage and ratio calculations.

observations: The Quant section is where the timer hurt most. Candidates who got stuck on the DI set lost time they could not recover, because the section locks at 15 minutes.
At least one centre had small desks, which made it awkward to handle the mouse and the rough sheet together.
No systemic technical problems were reported for this shift.
disagreements: English difficulty: most reviews rated it Moderate to Hard, but one listing rated it Easy and one candidate called it easy but long.
QUAD vs BRICS: one source places the QUAD question in this shift, while another says QUAD came in the 1:30 PM paper and BRICS in this one.
Overall good attempts: coaching tables say 82–85. Section-by-section estimates from video reviews add up nearer 78–82, which suggests the lower end is more realistic.

faqs.q: Was SSC CGL Shift 1 held on 30 September 2026?
faqs.a: No. The 10 AM slot had no exam at almost all centres. The first paper actually held was at 1:30 PM, which is why many sites call it 'Shift 1'.

faqs.q: Is there sectional timing in SSC CGL 2026 Tier 1?
faqs.a: Yes. Each of the four sections gets 15 minutes and locks when its time is up, so you cannot go back to it. On day 1 the order reported was Reasoning, GA, Quant, then English.

faqs.q: What is a safe score for SSC CGL 2026 Tier 1 after day 1?
faqs.a: Early estimates put a safe raw score for the general category at around 135–140 out of 200. This is only coaching-channel chatter. Tier 1 scores are normalised across all shifts, and SSC has not published any cut-off.

faqs.q: Will a tougher shift lower my final score?
faqs.a: No. SSC normalises scores across shifts, so candidates in a harder shift are not penalised compared with those in an easier one.
